transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in today is that I just can’t seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. Between work and everything else, there's just a lot to juggle—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions. And instead of figuring out how to prioritize it all, I just end up starting whatever is loudest at the moment, rather than what actually matters. I just can't seem to get a handle on it on my own anymore.
Have you struggled with this difficulty in organizing your tasks and staying on track since you were a child, or is this a relatively new challenge for you?

It's definitely not new. Looking back, I can see this was there in grade school, too. My teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but that I daydreamed a lot. I would actually finish my assignments and then just... forget to turn them in. Or I'd completely lose my homework folders. So, yeah, this was happening long before I was even a teenager.
When you were in grade school, did you find that you were often physically restless, like having trouble staying in your seat or feeling like you had to be constantly moving?

Not really when I was a kid, no. I wasn't the type to be bouncing around the classroom or getting in trouble for leaving my seat. 

But I do feel it now. Like, if I'm on a long design call for work, I start feeling this... this pressure building up in my body to get up. I usually end up pacing around my office, or I'll just keep shifting from chair to chair, even when I’m really trying to look focused on the meeting.
Aside from the restlessness you mentioned, do you often find yourself interrupting others while they are speaking or blurting out answers before a question is finished?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I might jump in sometimes if I get excited about an idea during a meeting, but I don't make a habit of cutting people off or blurting things out. I'm usually more of the quiet one, honestly, just trying to follow along with the conversation.
In the past six months, how often have you felt like you were 'on the go' or acting as if you were 'driven by a motor'?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really get that feeling of being driven by a motor. I mean, I have that physical restlessness I just mentioned when I'm stuck on a long call, but overall, I'm not really an 'on the go' kind of person. Most of the time I'm just sitting at my computer, trying to get my work done. So, no, I haven't felt like that.
